founded_year_range: 2011 (501(c)(3) PPDA 'founded in March 2011' per archived 2012 Mission and History page, confirmed; IRS exemption ruling date March 2018 per ProPublica; renamed Symptomatic/ATNS autumn 2024; neuroplastic.org 2026; Clarke's stress-illness approach dates to the 1980s, book 2007)
category: psychological/neuroplastic-pain therapy (nonprofit education, referral and advocacy hub)
cost_summary: 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Quiz and practitioner directory are free; Clarke's 12-chapter self-treatment course is described as free (no price on the course page). Rewiring Project membership starts at US$5.50/month (Community tier; ~$66/yr); professional tiers exist but prices are not published (checked site and archived 2025 membership page); first month free. 2026 conference registration price not posted (member discount); pre-conference workshops +$126. 2023 virtual conference was $375 with CE/CME or $275 without, 30% member discount (confirmed on Nov 2023 Wayback capture). Therapy from directory practitioners is billed separately at private rates.
mechanisms: neuroplastic/learned pain (brain-generated danger signal / predictive processing)
autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
mechanism_summary: ATNS calls these conditions "neuroplastic symptoms." The brain has learned a danger or alarm signal and keeps firing it, producing real pain or illness with no tissue damage behind it. Stress, unrecognised emotion and trauma (especially adverse childhood experiences) set it off. Personality habits such as perfectionism, people-pleasing and self-criticism keep it going, along with fear of the symptoms. The older PPDA protocol added Sarno-style psychodynamic ideas: symptoms express intolerable emotions somatically and distract from them. ATNS rejects Sarno's oxygen-deprivation hypothesis in favour of "learned neural pathways" that can be unlearned. It uses one mechanism for every condition ("Many Symptoms, One Brain"), from back pain to ME/CFS, long COVID, chronic Lyme, MCS, POTS and EDS, with a caveat to rule out structural disease first.
techniques: pain neuroscience education / diagnosis acceptance (learned brain pathway, not damage)
self-diagnosis quiz using exclusion plus positive criteria
referral to Pain Reprocessing Therapy (somatic tracking, safety reappraisal)
referral to Emotional Awareness and Expression Therapy
graded return to avoided activities / outcome independence
linking symptom onset to life stressors and ACEs
emotion identification, tolerance and expression (journaling, free-writing, role play, Gestalt empty chair, free association, dream interpretation)
addressing perfectionism, people-pleasing and self-criticism; self-compassion
peer community, monthly expert Q&As, local chapters
recommended books and apps (Unlearn Your Pain, Curable, Nervana)
mainstream_notes: Board members hold or held academic and health-system posts: Clarke (Kaiser Permanente NW gastroenterologist 1984-2009; OHSU emeritus), Schubiner (Michigan State/Ascension), Rashbaum (former; NYU Rusk TMS/Mind-Body), Kennedy (former; Kaiser Permanente NW long COVID). Conference carries accredited CE/CME (up to 17.75 h in 2026), and Clarke led two professional textbooks (2019, 2022). PPDA is listed as a funder of the JAMA Psychiatry PRT trial, which drew wide mainstream attention. No clinical guideline (NICE, CMS, AHRQ) recognises "neuroplastic symptoms" or PPD as a diagnosis or endorses ATNS. The organisation states it advocates to federal policymakers.
insurance_notes: Membership, conferences and courses are not reimbursable. Psychotherapy from licensed directory clinicians can be billed under standard psychotherapy codes; 49 of 155 directory listings say they accept insurance (Oct 2026). Recovery coaches are not covered.

key_trials.citation: Ashar YK, Gordon A, Schubiner H, Uipi C, et al., Wager TD. Effect of Pain Reprocessing Therapy vs Placebo and Usual Care for Patients With Chronic Back Pain. JAMA Psychiatry 2022;79(1):13-23
key_trials.design: RCT: PRT vs open-label placebo injection vs usual care, chronic back pain. Trial of affiliated therapy (PRT), not of ATNS itself; PPDA listed as a funder; ATNS co-founders (Gordon, Schubiner) and board member (Uipi) are co-authors
key_trials.finding: 66% (33/50) pain-free or nearly pain-free post-treatment after PRT vs 20% placebo and 10% usual care; effects maintained at 1 year (Hedges g -0.70 vs placebo); 5-year follow-up (JAMA Psychiatry 2025;82:1049, doi:10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2025.1844): PRT still had lower pain intensity than both controls

key_trials.citation: Lumley MA, Schubiner H, Lockhart NA, Kidwell KM, Harte SE, Clauw DJ, Williams DA. Emotional awareness and expression therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, and education for fibromyalgia: a cluster-randomized controlled trial. Pain 2017;158(12):2354-2363
key_trials.design: Cluster RCT (40 groups): EAET vs CBT vs education, fibromyalgia; trial of affiliated therapy (EAET)
key_trials.finding: EAET did not differ from education on the primary outcome (pain severity at 6 months); better than education on several secondary outcomes (d 0.29-0.45); vs CBT, lower FM symptoms and widespread pain and more >=50% pain reduction (22.5% vs 8.3%)

key_trials.citation: Yarns BC, Jackson NJ, Alas A, Melrose RJ, Lumley MA, Sultzer DL. Emotional Awareness and Expression Therapy vs Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Chronic Pain in Older Veterans. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(6):e2415842
key_trials.design: RCT: EAET vs CBT, older veterans (92% male) with chronic musculoskeletal pain; trial of affiliated therapy (EAET)
key_trials.finding: EAET superior on pain severity post-treatment and at 6 months; >=30% pain reduction 63% vs 17%, >=50% 35% vs 7% post-treatment

key_trials.citation: Donnino MW, Thompson GS, Mehta S, Paschali M, Howard P, Antonsen SB, et al. Psychophysiologic symptom relief therapy for chronic back pain: a pilot randomized controlled trial. PAIN Reports 2021;6(3):e959
key_trials.design: Pilot RCT: PSRT vs MBSR vs usual care, chronic back pain; trial of affiliated therapy (PSRT)
key_trials.finding: Greater RMDQ disability reduction with PSRT; pain-free at 26 weeks 63.6% PSRT (n=11) vs 25.0% MBSR vs 16.7% usual care

key_trials.citation: Hsu MC, Schubiner H, Lumley MA, Stracks JS, Clauw DJ, Williams DA. Sustained Pain Reduction Through Affective Self-awareness in Fibromyalgia: A Randomized Controlled Trial. J Gen Intern Med 2010;25(10):1064-1070
key_trials.design: RCT: affective self-awareness (1 physician consult + 3 weekly 2-h group sessions) vs waitlist, women with fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: Lower pain severity, better physical function and higher tender-point threshold at 6 months vs waitlist; >=30% pain reduction in 45.8% vs 0%

key_trials.citation: Donnino MW, Howard P, Mehta S, Silverman J, Cabrera MJ, Yamin JB, et al. Psychophysiologic Symptom Relief Therapy for Post-Acute Sequelae of Coronavirus Disease 2019. Mayo Clin Proc Innov Qual Outcomes 2023;7(4):337-348
key_trials.design: Uncontrolled single-arm interventional cohort, long COVID without objective organ injury (NCT04854772)
key_trials.finding: Mean SSS-8 somatic symptom score fell 10.9 points by 13 weeks (p<.001); dyspnea, fatigue, pain and brain fog also improved. No control group, no post-treatment follow-up

controversy: The self-assessment treats a lack of medical explanation as evidence of neuroplastic illness. The condition list ("nearly 500" symptoms) is very broad. It includes EDS, small fiber neuropathy, trigeminal and post-herpetic neuralgia, POTS, MCAS, interstitial cystitis, ME/CFS, long COVID and "chronic Lyme," which risks missed organic disease and draws objections from patient groups that it psychologises their illness. Claims that "most patients fully recover" go beyond the RCT data, which come mainly from back pain and fibromyalgia and include a null primary outcome for EAET vs education (Lumley 2017). An uncontrolled long COVID cohort (N=23) is promoted alongside RCTs. Screening and treatment content stresses ACEs and personality traits, which some patients may read as blame. Board members sell their own books, courses and therapy, and most trials were run by the therapies' developers. Prevalence ("1 in 3 adults", "80 million Americans") and cost ("$600B") figures come from the organisation's own non-peer-reviewed surveys and extrapolations. Disclosure: PPDA is a listed funder of the Boulder PRT trial, whose senior investigator is the survey author (Wager).

popularity.reach_estimate: About 300k-1M cumulative people reached. Basis: ~30k/month self-reported current reach (~360k/yr), lower in earlier years; thousands of conference, course and membership participants; >10k patients treated by board clinicians. Deep engagement (members, course takers, attendees) is probably in the low tens of thousands.
popularity.method_notes: Archived PPDA pages (2011 founding, 2012 conference, 2017 crowdfunding, 2023 conference prices) were re-checked on 2026-10-13. IRS 990 revenue (ProPublica) shows a small organisation: <$5k/yr 2014-16, ~$80-107k 2017-20, peak $335k 2022, $165k 2023. Reddit (r/TMSHealing) size, Google Trends and social follower counts could not be retrieved (Reddit blocks automated access; social pages require login). The trajectory is anchored on dated, documented events and 990 revenue: 2011 founding; 2012 website launch and NYAM conference (~250); 2013-2016 low activity; 2017 crowdfunding of the Boulder PRT trial; 2019 and 2022 textbooks; 2020s virtual CE/CME conferences; Sept 2021 JAMA Psychiatry PRT publication with heavy media coverage; 2023 long COVID content and first national survey; autumn 2024 rebrand to Symptomatic/ATNS; 2026 neuroplastic.org relaunch and Dallas conference. Current reach figures are self-reported by ATNS. Reach_log10 is an order-of-magnitude estimate of unique people exposed to its materials.
